text:
Adam Edstrom, all 6'7" of him, has gone from part-timer with the Rangers to everyday forward in Nashville. He plays 14:47 a night, up from 9:28 last season, has 84 hits in 20 games and 6 goals for a team that has won seven straight. Sports Illustrated even found room for his family this week ("Adam Edström’s Family Has a Different Definition of Hockey Night").

Our numbers flag it as a breakout, and the chances back it up. His own expected goals per 60 (the quality of chances he gets) is 1.27, up from 0.76, and 6 goals on 6.26 expected means there is nothing to give back. Nashville has 52.4% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 6.9 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, on just six games, had him getting 2.9 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net. The caveat is recent: he hasn't scored in his last six games and was held without a shot Friday, so the goals have cooled even as the role holds. Twenty games is still a small sample for a player this new to the job.
headline: Adam Edstrom's breakout has the chances behind it
